claim: RDS for SQL Server allows up to 15 read replicas from one source DB instance, but replication might lag when the source has more than 5 read replicas.
question: How many read replicas can an RDS for SQL Server source have, and when can lag appear?

values.spoken: lag can appear above five replicas

qualifiers.condition: Enterprise Edition only, on DB instance classes with four or more vCPUs

evidence.quote: Replication might lag when your source DB instance has more than 5 read replicas.
You can create up to 15 read replicas from one source DB instance.

claim: RDS for SQL Server read replicas are only available on the Enterprise Edition engine and on DB instance classes with four or more vCPUs.
question: What does RDS for SQL Server require before you can create read replicas?

values.display: only available on the SQL Server Enterprise Edition

evidence.quote: Read replicas are only available on the SQL Server Enterprise Edition (EE) engine.
Read replicas are only available for DB instances running on DB instance classes with four or more vCPUs.

claim: Automated backups occur daily during the preferred backup window, and a backup that needs more time continues after the window ends until it finishes.
question: How often does RDS take automated backups, and what if a backup runs past the window?

values.spoken: once a day in the backup window

qualifiers.scope: per DB instance or Multi-AZ DB cluster
qualifiers.condition: the backup window can't overlap the weekly maintenance window

evidence.quote: Automated backups occur daily during the preferred backup window.
If the backup requires more time than allotted to the backup window, the backup continues after the window ends until it finishes.

claim: For MariaDB, MySQL, Oracle and PostgreSQL in a Multi-AZ deployment, I/O isn't suspended on the primary during backup because the backup is taken from the standby; for SQL Server I/O is suspended briefly because the backup is taken from the primary.
question: Does an automated backup pause I/O on an RDS primary DB instance?

values.display: the backup is taken from the standby
values.spoken: Multi-AZ backups come from the standby

qualifiers.condition: Single-AZ instances can see a brief I/O suspension, typically under a few seconds

evidence.quote: For MariaDB, MySQL, Oracle, and PostgreSQL, I/O activity isn't suspended on your primary during backup for Multi-AZ deployments because the backup is taken from the standby.
For SQL Server, I/O activity is suspended briefly during backup for both Single-AZ and Multi-AZ deployments because the backup is taken from the primary.
